messages:
jess: dropped a new prototype for the pool dropdown — focus is on reducing scan time and clarifying burst copy: https://figma.com/file/new-proto

anya: watched it. suggestion: replace the flat list with a small "Priority strip" at the top (3 items) + the full list below. makes common pools one-tap.

mike: API note: we can return an ordered preferredPools array per org. small change and stable IDs required if UI reorders things.

jess: nice. copy: for the SLO chip on selected pool, i'd prefer human labels like "Low latency" vs raw ms. more friendly.

omar: a11y: chips must have aria-labels like "Pool: low-latency, SLO: low" and accessible contrast >=4.5:1. avoid color-only meaning.

lee: about "Burst" — customers ask if it's extra billed. propose label: "Burst capacity (time-limited)" + a help icon linking to billing. short tooltip: "Temporary GPUs during spikes — billed at standard rates."

khalid: slider accessibility: provide keyboard stepper fallback and an aria-live announcement on change: "Latency target: Balanced. Cost: Medium." keep it concise (<60 chars).

jess: agreed. also change min/max labels to "Min active GPUs" and "Max active GPUs" and ensure programmatic association with inputs.

omar: clamp behavior: if requested min > pool max show inline red message and SR announcement: "Min adjusted to pool max: 4." short and explicit.

mike: implementation constraint: some pool caps are sourced from another service; client should cache caps for ~2 minutes to limit calls. I'll add this to the API ticket.

nora: small UX nit: in compact view collapse the priority strip to icons only with accessible long-press/focus labels. keep focus ring visible.

anya: good work. next steps: jess to update frames with priority strip + SLO wording + burst help copy, mike to confirm API change and caching, omar & khalid to review a11y tokens. i'll draft canary notes for the rollout.

jess: will post updated frames tomorrow AM. thanks all :thumbsup:
